subject: targetRunner Segmentation Fault - more than two numbers!

messages.author: 4ddd2d2e063a3076
messages.subject: targetRunner Segmentation Fault - more than two numbers!
parts:
Hi all,
I am really new on irace but very much interested in using it for my research.

I need to tune some parameters of a C++ algorithm I coded. 
My algorithm is normally executed in the following way: ./algorithm.exe instance.dat seed list_of_irace_parameters stdout_file
where the output of my algorithm (a column of numbers) is collected and saved in the stdout file that will be called in the target-runner.
 
I set up all things for irace. In particular the target-runner executable has been modified as follows:

EXE=~/tuning/algorithm.exe


STDOUT=c${CONFIG_ID}-${INSTANCE_ID}.stdout


$EXE $INSTANCE $SEED ${CONFIG_PARAMS} ${STDOUT}


When I call irace to perform the racing I get back the following error message:

Errore: == irace == The output of targetRunner should not be more than two numbers!

== irace == The call to targetRunner was:

/home/anna/tuning/target-runner 1 1 986808085 /home/tuning/Instances/instance.dat --A 50 --B 5 --C 10

== irace == The output was:

/home/anna/tuning/target-runner: line 44: 31640 Segmentation fault     

 (core dumped) $EXE $INSTANCE ${SEED} ${CONFIG_PARAMS} ${STDOUT} 



Moreover, the stdout file is not created (I checked and when used alone my algorithm is able to open it save columns and save it), other empty files are generated.
I have temporally deleted the STDERR because it was causing me other errors.

I cannot understand where that segmentation fault comes from. As suggested in the manual If I copy the command and execute it directly in the ExecDir I get the same message as well. 

I have also tried to create a stdout file by myself (let's say X.stdout) and write in it a column of numbers. Providing in the target-runner STDOUT=X-stdout the commands are able to extract just the last number in the column. But the error message of the Segmentation fault persists!

If you have any suggestion I would be very happy,

Have a nice evening,
A.

messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: targetRunner Segmentation Fault - more than two numbers!
parts:
Dear Anna,

As the error says, this is often a problem with either the target-runner or algorithm.exe and not a bug in irace. In this case, I think the problem is probably algorithm.exe because the segfault mentions that line. One quick test would be to add:

echo $EXE $INSTANCE $SEED ${CONFIG_PARAMS} ${STDOUT} >> c${CONFIG_ID}-${INSTANCE_ID}.log

before calling $EXE, so that you know what target-runner is actually executing. Run irace again (you can do a quick run with --check). If that fails, then look in the .log file of the call to target-runner that failed and try to run that exact command from within execDir.

Some transient bugs (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisenbug) are only visible when running within irace and not when running exactly the same command outside irace. They are typically pointer/uninitialized memory issues. Look at the user guide, Appendix B item 7 (in the latest version). There are some tips on how to debug those using valgrind. For better or worse, irace is extremely good at finding bugs in programs :)

Cheers,

Manuel.

messages.author: 4ddd2d2e063a3076
messages.subject: Re: targetRunner Segmentation Fault - more than two numbers!
parts:
Thank you Manuel so much,

the problem has been solved.
It was just a flag in the parameter file that was not "accepted" by my algorithm.

Have a nice day,
A.
